skills.name: collar-full-shake
skills.purpose: Use a validated shirt-collar grasp to lift, shake open, transport, and lay the garment down so the collar structure can reveal the garment.
skills.guidance: Use only after the visual collar decision and grounded Camera A grasp are validated. Keep the collar grasp orientation fixed and perpendicular to the collar. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, center at Y=0, perform the host-owned shake-open maneuver, then move toward a useful +X location before retreating toward -X while descending through several waypoints. Keep descent and retreat balanced rather than making either one dominate, release only near the table after the garment has had room to spread, and retract/home afterward. Use current measured geometry and controller IK; never copy fixed coordinates, release in mid-air, or replace the collar with a shoulder or sleeve.

skills.name: controller-ik-recovery
skills.purpose: Recover safely when controller IK rejects a garment manipulation path before physical execution.
skills.guidance: When controller IK rejects a pose or interpolated segment, preserve the supported visual objective but shorten extreme reach, lift, or transport; keep every waypoint inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and controller IK before execution.

skills.name: direct-shake
skills.purpose: Test whether a validated garment grasp can open the cloth by lifting and shaking it without running the collar-specific transport and laydown routine.
skills.guidance: Use after any grounded fabric grasp when the immediate experiment is only a shake response test. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, keep the held fabric clear of the table, center if useful, run the host-owned shake maneuver, observe whether the garment separates or reveals structure, then lower and release in a controlled way. Do not add a long +X retreat or pretend that a shake-only result proves collar identity; preserve workspace, grounding, preflight, and IK checks and never use fixed coordinates.

skills.name: flatten-garment
skills.purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment by validating the grasped structure, establishing a useful hanging configuration, transporting in a verified opening direction, and laying down only while the scene shows measurable improvement.
skills.guidance:
Follow this staged workflow:
1. Acquire a validated garment structure: choose a visible, liftable anchor whose local RGB-D measurement, height, and depth consistency support a real garment grasp; do not proceed from an unsupported or table-only point.
2. Establish a hanging configuration if useful: lift to a validated safe height and confirm that the grasped fabric is supported and can hang without dragging or colliding. If the lift does not reveal a supported structure, stop and re-plan.
3. Transport toward a verified opening direction: infer the direction from the current garment geometry and before/after evidence, then use validated intermediate waypoints with stable orientation and workspace margin. The farthest safe X direction is allowed only when the scene verifies that it opens the garment; do not assume it is always correct.
4. Continue only while overlap decreases or coverage increases: after each meaningful transport segment, compare the garment footprint, visible area, layer overlap, and height relief. Stop, release, or re-plan when the move is not improving those measures; never continue a blind pull.
5. Lay down progressively: retreat while descending through validated intermediate heights, release quasi-statically on a clean surface, and avoid dropping, flinging, twisting, or dragging the loaded gripper. The skill supplies this decision sequence, never fixed coordinates or robot API calls.

skills.name: grounding-plan-recovery
skills.purpose: Recover from an invalid or inconsistent grounded garment proposal before motion.
skills.guidance: When grounding validation rejects a selected point or its use in the plan, reinspect the current evidence, choose a newly grounded visible fabric point, keep the path inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

skills.name: hold-checkpoint-timeout-recovery
skills.purpose: Interpret and recover from a garment run whose post-grasp hold verification could not be classified in time and therefore forced a local release, and recognize when 15 consecutive acquisition failures across diverse anchor classes with adequate depth definitively disprove single-anchor separation for a configuration and require infrastructure escalation.
skills.guidance: Keep the existing rules: a failed-closed or timed-out hold check makes the observation evidence about the grasp only, the unexecuted transport must never be recorded as wrong in direction or distance, and the validated approach clearance, deposit region and quasi-static release carry over to the retry. Add this definitive escalation threshold with infrastructure acknowledgment: when a configuration has produced 15 or more consecutive acquisition failures across at least 5 geometrically distinct anchor classes (peaks, boundary bands, low-relief structures, raised rims, corners, raised edges, claimed free boundary lips) where adequate engagement depth was achieved (closure commanded at or below measured surface height, including compression-probe-recommended depths for high-relief structures and manual calculation for low-relief structures) and every attempt confirms no independent hanging material with all far landmarks remaining seated and hold checkpoint returning FAILED_CLOSED or timeout, treat this as definitive evidence that the garment configuration does not provide separable single-anchor structure. At that threshold, escalate to a two-contact strategy where one contact immobilizes a region through weight, pinning, or clamping while the second contact attempts separation, or target a mechanically verified free edge where the gripper can wrap around a confirmed fabric boundary with visible interior passage or light between plies on both sides. The critical insight: when high-relief structures (17+mm raised edges), medium-relief ridges (10+mm), low-relief corners (sub-4mm and 7mm range), raised plateau tents, compressed peaks, and claimed free boundary lips with adequate depth and varied entry axes (vertical, oblique, side) all produce identical empty-jaws outcomes, the anchor class variety itself and the entry axis variety have both been exhausted. State the infrastructure limitation explicitly when available primitives cannot execute true two-contact opposition: acknowledge that continuing single-anchor attempts is unsafe and ungrounded, and that no further safe grounded experiment is possible within current primitive constraints rather than attempting a 16th single-anchor variant. Preserve validated approach clearance, deposit region, planned pull direction and quasi-static release across the strategy change, since unexecuted transport carries no evidence about those choices.

skills.name: laydown
skills.purpose: Convert a garment held from a useful lifting anchor into a more spread tabletop configuration, and recognise when a release has re-piled the garment onto itself instead of opening it.
skills.guidance: Keep the quasi-static procedure: let the garment hang under gravity, retreat away from the hanging cloth while descending through intermediate heights, let the hanging face become the upward face, and release in a controlled way. Add two checks. First, before descending, require the retreat to carry the grasp point beyond the horizontal extent of the material still hanging below it, onto clear table, so the fabric unrolls onto bare surface rather than settling back over the area it came from; a retreat shorter than the hanging garment's own reach should be treated as not ready for release. Second, after release, compare footprints rather than only position: if the deposited outline sits inside the previous outline, if previously exposed features such as prints, collars or hems have become covered, and if new steep fold walls appear in depth, judge the laydown a regression caused by too short a retreat, and plan the next deposit farther out across clean table instead of repeating the same descent from the same anchor.

skills.name: molmo-annotation-retry
skills.purpose: Recover from an auxiliary Molmo annotation worker failure before motion.
skills.guidance: When auxiliary Molmo annotation fails before execution, preserve the saved perception evidence, retry the annotation on a fresh iteration, and never treat a missing semantic anchor as garment-state evidence; keep workspace, release, preflight, and IK validation mandatory before any later motion.

skills.name: null-change-missed-grasp-recovery
skills.purpose: Recognise a near-null garment action, separate a clean miss from a contact-without-hold on a compressible pile, and additionally reject a closure whose resolved anchor or engaged height is inconsistent with the visually chosen structure.
skills.guidance: Keep the existing null-change and contact-without-hold checks and the escalation rule. Add a pre-closure consistency gate. Before the jaws close, confirm that the anchor the controller actually resolved corresponds to the structure that was chosen in the images, and that the engaged height falls inside the measured relief of that structure rather than collapsing onto the table plane. If the resolved contact point sits far from the visually selected feature, or if the engaged height is indistinguishable from the surrounding tabletop, treat the planned bite as ungrounded and re-ground before descending instead of executing it. Likewise, a local surface measurement taken at a different location, outside the working region, or on bare table is not grounding for the anchor and must not be used to justify a closure. When the resulting observation is a complete null change with every far landmark seated, record it as evidence about the anchor and the engagement geometry only, leave the untested pull direction, pull distance, deposit region and release choices intact, and make the next attempt at a differently structured opening rather than repeating the same descent.

skills.name: planning-timeout-recovery
skills.purpose: Recover from a Claude planning timeout before any garment motion starts.
skills.guidance: When planning times out before execution, retain the exact failure context, start a fresh planning attempt from saved perception, keep all waypoints inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

skills.name: preflight-contract-recovery
skills.purpose: Recover from a rejected action schema or unsafe action sequence before motion.
skills.guidance: When static preflight rejects a plan, keep only the high-level garment objective, correct the reported action contract or sequence, keep all waypoints inside the workspace, include an explicit release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

skills.name: sleeve-fold-carry-sufficiency
skills.purpose: Detect and correct the local-curl sleeve fold failure, where a sleeve grasp is real but the carry is shorter than the sleeve's own reach, producing a near-null fixed-view change.
skills.guidance: After a sleeve-in fold attempt, compare the fixed collar-up view before and after. If every far landmark (collar ring, opposite sleeve, hem and body edges, chest print) is exactly seated and the only difference is a small retraction or curl of the grasped sleeve tip, with no new ply boundary over the chest and no newly covered print, classify the run as a carry-distance failure rather than a direction or target error. On retry: bite the outermost cuff hem band so the sleeve hinges at the armhole; require planned horizontal carry at least equal to the measured cuff-to-armhole span so the grasp point ends beyond the hanging sleeve's reach and past the garment centerline; take a mid-transport confirmation still and abort or re-ground if the sleeve silhouette has not begun to swing; descend and release quasi-statically over the chest band only after that clearance is met. Do not re-tune pull direction, deposit region or release timing after a local-curl outcome, since those were never exercised, and keep grounding, workspace, IK and preflight checks mandatory.

skills.name: sleeve-fold-carry-sufficiency-confirmed
skills.purpose: Confirm a successful inward sleeve fold and record the carry-sufficiency criterion that distinguishes it from the local-curl failure mode.
skills.guidance: Grasp the outermost cuff hem band so the sleeve hinges at the armhole, and plan a horizontal carry at least equal to the measured cuff-to-armhole span so the grasp point finishes past the garment centerline. Confirm success in the fixed collar-up view with four joint signatures: (1) bare table newly exposed where the sleeve lay, (2) the garment-side outline straightening from a sleeve lobe to an armhole-level edge, (3) a new ply boundary showing the stitched cuff hem over the chest band, and (4) partial covering of a previously exposed chest feature such as a print. If instead every far landmark is seated and only the cuff tip curls, classify as carry-distance failure and lengthen the carry rather than re-tuning direction or deposit. Residual bunching of the deposited cuff ply indicates the release was slightly short of or above the intended chest band; correct by releasing closer to the centerline at lower height, not by re-choosing the anchor.

skills.name: translation-only-reanchor
skills.purpose: Recognize when repeated congruent relocations disprove single-anchor peeling for a garment, and additionally retire the terminal end-cap of a rolled bundle as a ply anchor once a perpendicular carry only relocates the whole bundle.
skills.guidance: Keep the existing stop rule, the free-boundary verification requirement, and the mandatory lift-phase abort. Add this appearance lesson: the rounded end of an elongated cloth roll, even when it presents solid measurable relief above the table and reads as an end-of-structure boundary with a visible tuck, is not evidence of a separable ply. A roll end is continuous with the body, so carrying it across the table perpendicular to the roll axis relocates the whole bundle instead of paying wound fabric out, and the distal lobe travels with the gripper rather than staying seated. Treat such an outcome as two separate findings: the grounding, engagement depth, approach clearance, fixed wrist orientation and quasi-static release are validated because cloth was held and carried and must be reused unchanged, while the terminal end-cap joins the retired anchor classes alongside the high-relief core, the planar raised shelf, the flat perimeter lip and the steep fold wall. Do not re-tune pull direction or pull distance after such a result, since no layer was isolated and the carry tested nothing. Require either a mechanically verified free fabric boundary with visible interior passage between plies, or opposition supplied by immobilizing material well away from the separation point, before the next lift. Also treat a deposit that lands back over a feature the previous view had exposed as an unhelpful laydown, and place the next deposit farther out on clear surface.

skills.name: wrist-lift-still-diagnosticity
skills.purpose: Prevent treating a fabric-flooded wrist-camera lift still as proof of acquisition, and define what a lift still must contain to classify hold versus miss.
skills.guidance: A wrist-mounted Camera A frame taken after a commanded lift is diagnostic only if it shows at least two of: (a) a jaw/fingertip silhouette in contact with a pinched ply, (b) background table visible UNDER the held fabric with a clear gap or cast shadow, (c) a tented/draped fabric contour hanging below the grasp point. A frame whose field of view is simply filled by fabric, even fabric showing a recognisable feature such as a stitched cuff hem, proves only that the wrist is near cloth; since the camera moves with the gripper, framing change is not cloth motion. When such a non-diagnostic still is combined with a fixed-view before/after that is congruent in every far landmark, record the outcome as UNKNOWN acquisition (not confirmed empty grasp, not carry-distance failure), leave pull direction, pull distance, deposit region and release untouched as untested, and on retry command the post-lift still at a pose/tilt that guarantees table background beneath the held ply, aborting the transport if that gap is absent.
